items.summary:
On November 10, 2026, we released versions 19.5.4, 19.4.6, 19.3.8 for GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition. These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to
one of these versions immediately.
GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already running a patched version. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated customers do not need to take action. GitLab releases fixes for vulnerabilities in patch releases. There are two types of patch releases:
scheduled releases and ad-hoc critical patches for high-severity vulnerabilities. Scheduled releases are released twice a month on the second and fourth Wednesdays.
For more information, please visit our releases handbook and security FAQ .
You can see all of GitLab release blog posts here . We are committed to ensuring that all aspects of GitLab that are exposed to customers or that host customer data are held to
the highest security standards. To maintain good security hygiene, it is highly recommended that all customers
upgrade to the latest patch release for their supported version. You can read more best practices in securing your GitLab instance in our blog post. Recommended Action We strongly recommend that all installations running a version affected by the issues described below are upgraded to the latest version as soon as possible . When no specific deployment type (omnibus, source code, helm chart, etc.) of a product is mentioned, it means all types are affected. Important guidance for self-compiled GitLab installations: The fix for CVE-2026-105437 is a patch to Git. Official GitLab Linux packages and container images already include the patched Git. For self-compiled installations, follow the Update Gitaly steps, which rebuild the Git binaries embedded in Gitaly. You must also rebuild the Git installation referenced by git.bin_path in config/gitlab.yml from the matching Gitaly stable branch, as described in Git . If that Git comes from your distribution’s package instead, upgrade it to 2.56.1 or later, or to a version your distribution has patched for CVE-2026-105437. Security fixes Table of security fixes Title Severity CVE-2026-105437 (vulnerability in git ) Critical CVE-2026-105437 (vulnerability in git ) This release addresses the security issue CVE-2026-105437 , a heap-based buffer overflow in git , by updating the version of git bundled with GitLab. This issue has been remediated on GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, and in GitLab CE/EE versions 19.3.8, 19.4.6, and 19.5.4. In GitLab, under certain conditions, this vulnerability in git can result in out-of-bounds heap writes, which could be used to execute arbitrary commands within GitLab’s Gitaly environment. Impacted Versions: GitLab CE/EE: all versions from 16.2 before 19.3.8, 19.4 before 19.4.6, and 19.5 before 19.5.4 Thanks taise for reporting this vulnerability through our HackerOne bug bounty program. Bug fixes 19.5.4 [19.5] Update danger-review component to 2.2.0 backup: Bump gocloud.dev to v0.47.0 for S3-compatible backup sink (19-5-stable backport) ci: Package on the omnibus branch matching the MR target (19-5-stable backport) ci: Use MR target branch directly for omnibus package trigger (19-5-stable) Backport of ‘Back off StoreScansWorker retries on lease contention’ to 19.5 Backport of ‘Stop event purges from moving the stale scan cursor’ to 19.5 Backport of ‘Fail closed when OpenBao login returns a non-JSON body’ [19.5] Use the system CA bundle for gRPC default roots Restore the full coding environment for recommend_reviewers Backport of ‘Add 19.5 release note for GitLab Orbit GA’ Backport of ‘Fail early when an API-only flow’s image has no curl’ Backport of ‘Stop failing on stale browser console allowlist specs’ into 19.5 Backport of ‘Read top-level dependency ancestors from direct graph edges’ into 19.5 Backport of ‘Stop traversing full dependency graph on ingestion’ into 19.5 Backport of “Fix use_legacy_view? for organi
